analysis.title: Rates Spark: Kevin Warsh and John Healey walk into a bar
key_insights: ING expects the Fed to leave rates unchanged at the 28 October FOMC unless there is a Brazilian-style election surprise.

The US 10yr yield has been holding near 4.99%, just under 5%. ING expects it to snap back above 5% because inflation, the fiscal deficit and AI-boom-related impulses remain in play, though timing is uncertain.

A very dovish Warsh would validate the break below 5%, a very hawkish Warsh without an actual hike would push the 10yr back above 5%, and anything in between, the most likely outcome, would leave it where it is.

The Fed is unlikely to set out a plan to shrink its balance sheet at this meeting. ING expects committee recommendations closer to the turn of the year. Shrinking the balance sheet remains a policy objective for Chair Warsh.
ING estimates a political risk premium of about 20bp in the 10yr gilt yield, versus close to zero a few months ago. A boring UK Autumn Budget could unwind up to 20bp of it.
Gilt auction results are holding up better than before last year's Budget. Last week's 10yr auction and Tuesday's 6yr auction both showed healthy demand.
Global factors, especially energy prices at new highs, remain the bigger driver of sterling rates than the Budget.
Early UK elections could be the next surprise for markets. ING notes France showed that markets value political stability more than the exact fiscal deficit figure.
Liquidity conditions are stable and repo is behaving far better than a year ago.

macro_indicators.reading: about 4.99%, below 5%, after an earlier break above 5.25%
macro_indicators.interpretation: The yield is hovering just under 5%. ING expects a move back above 5% over time, driven by inflation, the fiscal deficit and AI-boom-related impulses.
ING's base case is no change, with a softer approach from the FOMC following the recent rally in Treasuries.
ING's estimate. A boring Budget could remove up to 20bp from 10yr gilt yields, while a spending splurge would turn the story bearish.

risk_factors: A UK spending splurge at the Autumn Budget would compound energy-related inflation fears and push gilt yields higher.
Early UK elections or a reopening of the political battleground could make investors more cautious on gilts.
A very hawkish Warsh without an actual hike could push the US 10yr back above 5%.
Inflation, the fiscal deficit and AI-boom-related impulses keep upward pressure on US yields.
geopolitical: UK political risk: possible early elections and uncertainty around Burnham's ambitions.
Energy prices are hitting new highs, feeding inflation fears.
A Brazilian election surprise is named as a possible disruption to the Fed's plans.
